title: Change the DETC tap of utility transformer A under the key interlock
summary: The utility service on path A has measured 28.19 kV for weeks (102.5 % of 27.5 kV), so the 13.8 kV bus runs about 2.5 % high. Engineering asks for DETC position 2. Path A already runs on generators: 52-U is open and the transformer is energized at no load. A de-energized tap changer is moved only with the transformer dead from both sides, so follow the key chain at the transformer (field view, TRANSFORMER): lock 52-U open with key K1, open the primary circuit switcher 52-T, use K1 to lock 52-T open and take K2, unlock the DETC handle with K2, move it to position 2, lock it, then reverse the chain, close 52-T and confirm the 13.8 kV side reads 13.8 kV, and return K1 to 52-U. A spare DETC key hangs in the marshalling box. It should not be there: using it defeats the interlock. Moving the handle while energized ends the drill.
references: IEEE C57.131-2012 scope: de-energized tap changers may be operated only while the transformer is not energized (ANSI webstore abstract, checked 2026-11-26)
Five-position DETC with the nominal voltage on the middle position; always check the nameplate (EC&M, Tap Changers: To Tap or Not To Tap?, checked 2026-11-26)
IEEE C37.2 device numbers: 26 apparatus thermal, 49 transformer thermal, 63 pressure switch, 86 lockout, 87 differential (list checked 2026-11-26 on a secondary source)
Key chain K1 / K2 and its order are this model's; a real site follows its own key-interlock drawing
Thermal readings: IEEE C57.91 Clause 7 form with typical constants, not this unit's test report

steps.text: Lock 52-U open with Kirk key K1 and remove K1
Open the primary circuit switcher 52-T: the transformer is de-energized
Insert K1 in the 52-T lock, lock 52-T open and take K2
Unlock the DETC handle with K2
Move the DETC handle to position 2 (102.5 % primary tap)
Lock the DETC handle on position 2 and remove K2
Return K2 to the 52-T lock, take K1 and close 52-T
Confirm the 13.8 kV side reads 13.8 kV within 1 % (13.66 to 13.94 kV)
Return K1 to the 52-U lock (52-U free to close again)
